title: The Last Ball
prompt: A bag contains 20 blue balls and 14 red balls. Each round: draw two balls at random, then follow this rule — if both are the same colour, put one blue ball back; if they're different colours, put one red ball back. Repeat until one ball remains.
What colour is the last ball?
hints: Track what happens to the count of red balls in each possible draw.
Drawing two red balls: red count goes from R to R-2. Drawing two blue: red count stays at R. Drawing one of each: red count stays at R. Notice anything?
The number of red balls never increases and only ever changes by 2. What does that imply if you start with 14 red balls?
solution_lede:
Rather than tracking both colours, focus only on the red balls. Let's see how R (the number of red balls) changes after each draw:

Both blue → put blue back: R stays the same.
Both red → put blue back: R decreases by 2.
One red, one blue → put red back: R stays the same.

Critically, R either stays constant or drops by exactly 2. It can never become odd if it starts even. Starting with 14 red balls (even), the red count stays even throughout. When only one ball remains, the red count is either 0 (ball is blue) or 1 (ball is red). Since R can't become 1 from an even start, the last ball must be blue.

If you start with an odd number of red balls (e.g., 13), the last ball is red by the same reasoning.

solution_steps.body: Observe: drawing two reds reduces R by 2. All other draws leave R unchanged. R never changes by an odd number.
Starting with R = 14 (even), R remains even throughout the entire process.
When one ball remains, R is either 0 or 1. Since R can't reach 1 from an even start, R must be 0.
R = 0 means no red balls remain. The last ball is blue.
